test: Restrict to kind='new' quotes with a final status (exclude blank). Per estimator (>=100 quotes) compute raw hit rate (won/all). Then compute an expected hit rate for each quote from customer x year cell rates (leave-one-estimator-out where possible) and compare observed vs expected per estimator (indirect standardisation); also within customer-year cells shared by several estimators. Check sampling noise via binomial SE. Then compare price per estimated hour and lead weeks for similar parts (same customer/family/year) between low- and high-hit estimators.
support: Adjusted gaps (observed minus expected) between estimators with >=100 quotes still exceed 5 points and are several standard errors from zero; low-hit estimators quote higher price per est hour or longer lead weeks within the same customer-year.
weaken: Adjusted gaps shrink below 5 points or within ~2 SE once customer and year are controlled; or estimators are assigned by customer so there is little overlap to compare.
expect: Moderate expectation that much of the raw gap is mix (estimator 118 in 2021-2022, customer assignment) but that some gap of 3-8 points survives for at least one estimator; maybe 50% that a >5 point adjusted gap survives with significance. Price/lead differences I expect to be small.
